The statement acknowledges a large adverse real shock and tightening global financial conditions, which the literature views as capable of amplifying downturns via credit channels and balance-sheet effects; for example, the financial accelerator and credit view suggest that weakened firm cash flows and bank capital raise external finance premia and depress investment, especially for smaller firms (Gertler and Gilchrist; Oliner and Rudebusch). In line with this, the FOMC’s cut to the effective lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS (QE), expanded repos, discount-window easing, and dollar swap lines are textbook measures to restore market functioning and support the flow of credit, thereby mitigating amplification and supporting aggregate demand. With inflation below target, forward-looking frameworks for stabilization (e.g., inflation-forecast targeting per Svensson) and operating at the zero lower bound point to the usefulness of QE and liquidity backstops to anchor expectations and reduce funding stress. Overall tone: negative due to the pandemic shock, but partially offset by aggressive, literature-consistent policy support.
